title: Sustainability and Human Impact
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Sustainability and Human Impact Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Sustainability of systems: bioaccumulation and biomagnification, human impacts on ecosystems, biodiversity and succession, climate change effects, and First Peoples knowledge and sustainable practices. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 9, Earth and Space Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 science worksheets (BC): biodiversity, pollution and bioaccumulation, human impact on ecosystems, carbon footprints and sustainable practices. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Sustainable use meets our needs and leaves enough for the future.
key_sub: Toxins build up as they move up food chains.
body_html:
How to think about it

Bioaccumulation is when a toxin, such as mercury or a pesticide, builds up in an organism over time. Biomagnification is when it becomes more concentrated at each step up a food chain, so top predators such as orcas and eagles have the most.

Human activities such as habitat loss, pollution, over-harvesting and climate change reduce biodiversity. Sustainable practices, including many First Peoples practices such as taking only what is needed, help keep ecosystems healthy.

Example

Why do orcas have high levels of toxins?

They are at the top of the food chain.

Answer: biomagnification

Example

What is a carbon footprint?

Greenhouse gases

Answer: the greenhouse gases caused by a person or activity

Common mistakes

  • Thinking toxins break down quickly in animals.
  • Thinking only big events harm ecosystems.
  • Mixing up bioaccumulation (one organism) and biomagnification (up the chain).

items.q: Olivia reads: “A hurricane knocks down many trees.” Is this a change to a physical (nonliving) or biological (living) part of the ecosystem?
items.e: Physical parts include water, soil, temperature and fire; biological parts are living things.

items.q: Liam learns: A disease killed many bats. What happened to the night-flying insects?
c: They increased because fewer bats ate them.
items.e: A change to one part of an ecosystem affects other populations.

items.q: What is a climate change indicator?

items.e: Indicators are tracked over many years to show trends.

items.q: Which technology is designed to reduce this impact: landfill chemicals leaking into groundwater?

items.q: Which is an example of adapting to climate change rather than slowing it?

switching from coal to wind power
items.e: Mitigation reduces the cause; adaptation reduces the damage.

items.q: Why does growing beans, peas or clover help the next crop?
c: they make the soil more acidic for good
they block all sunlight from weeds
they remove all water from the soil
bacteria in their roots fix nitrogen, which fertilizes the soil
items.e: Legumes reduce the need for synthetic fertilizer.
